- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.6) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 2–5% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from 10-day mean), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast at +2% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.0–0.17) and price is trending up, model underestimates continuation — add 1–3% to forecast for next 5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days) — increase forecast by 1–3% for first 5 days if sentiment is positive.
- When sentiment turns negative after a positive spike, model fails to adjust downward — reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days if sentiment drops below -0.2.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias — if price is above 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3 days if sentiment is weak or negative.
- If sentiment is consistently low (e.g., -0.3 to -0.6 over 5 days), model tends to underestimate true price — add 2–4% to forecast for next 5 days.
- Model often lags sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns positive after 3–5 days, forecast should adjust upward by 1–2% per day for next 3 days.
